text:
I need help with the narrative section of a grant application. I'm the director of a volunteer-run food bank in a town of about 9,000 people, and we're applying to our county community foundation for a refrigerated van.

What I have:
- We hand out about 38,000 pounds of food a month to 610 households. About 6,000 pounds of that is fresh produce, milk and eggs.
- Last summer, local farms offered us roughly 9,000 pounds of produce over three months that we had to turn down because we had no way to pick it up cold or store it.
- The van costs $68,000. We're asking the foundation for $50,000 and covering the other $18,000 from our reserves, which would leave us with $11,000.
- We have 23 regular volunteers. Four of them have said they would drive the van on a weekly schedule.
- The foundation gave us $12,000 for shelving in 2023. Our final report on that grant was four months late.

I want the narrative to say the van will let us double the amount of fresh food we hand out in the first year. The narrative is limited to 500 words.

Before I draft, there are a few things I need to know. The first matters most.

1. **What backs up "double the fresh food in the first year"?** You hand out 6,000 lb of fresh food a month, about 72,000 lb a year, so doubling it means roughly 72,000 lb more. The produce you turned down last summer comes to about 9,000 lb, which would be an increase of around 12%. Do you have other cold sources lined up that the van would open up, like grocery store pickups, a regional food bank's fresh allocation or dairy donations? Roughly how many pounds could they add? If they won't get you near double, I'd suggest a smaller target the reviewers can check against your numbers. A claim they can easily disprove could cost you the grant.

2. **Where will the cold food be stored?** You said you couldn't pick produce up cold or store it. A van fixes the pickup problem but not the storage. Do you already have walk-in or cooler space? Or would the food go straight from the van to distribution?

3. **What will the van cost to run each year, and who pays?** I mean insurance, fuel, maintenance and registration. Also, how many months of operating costs does $11,000 cover? Reviewers will want to know you can keep the van on the road and stay solvent after spending down your reserves.

4. **Why was the 2023 report late, and what has changed since then?** The foundation will remember it, so I'd mention it briefly and explain what's different now, such as a named person responsible for reports or a calendar reminder. Tell me what's actually true. If nothing has changed, say so, and we'll work out how to handle it.

5. **Do you have anything firm from the farms or the drivers?** For example, letters or emails from farms saying they'll give again next season, or tonnage estimates from them. On the driver side, do the four volunteers need a special licence or an insurance check to drive a van this size, and does each one have a set day?

If you don't know some of these, just say so. I'll write the narrative without that piece and won't fill the gap with a guess.

1. Fair point. No other cold sources lined up that I know of. I'll go with what the numbers support, so use a smaller target.

2. I don't know. I'd have to check.

3. Insurance and fuel come to about $4,500 a year. That isn't in our budget yet. I don't know the maintenance or registration costs, or exactly how many months the $11,000 covers.

4. The treasurer at that time was in the hospital for most of those four months. Our treasurer now is Dave Lin. I can name him as the person responsible for the final report, due 30 days after the grant year ends. I can also commit to sending the foundation our fresh food pounds every quarter.

5. Two of the farms have written letters saying they'll give again if we can pick up cold. I can't promise they'll offer the same 9,000 pounds again. I don't know about licences or insurance checks for the drivers, or whether they have set days.

I've written it to the 9,000-pound goal the numbers support. It's about 420 words, so you have some room left. There are two blanks in brackets for your organization's name and the county, and one bracketed sentence about running costs that only you can fill in.

<final_document>
[Food Bank Name] is asking the [County] Community Foundation for $50,000 toward a $68,000 refrigerated van. We will cover the remaining $18,000 from our own reserves.

**Who we serve**

Every month our volunteers hand out about 38,000 pounds of food to 610 households in our town of about 9,000 people. Only about 6,000 pounds of that is fresh produce, milk and eggs.

**The problem**

Fresh food is available to us, but we have no way to collect it. Last summer, local farms offered us about 9,000 pounds of produce over three months. We had to turn all of it down because we had no way to pick it up and keep it cold.

**What the van will do**

A refrigerated van will let us collect perishable donations directly from farms and keep them cold on the way back. Two of the farms that offered produce last summer have written letters saying they will give again once we can pick up cold. Those letters are attached.

**What we expect in the first year**

Our goal is to bring in the roughly 9,000 pounds of produce we had to refuse last year. That would raise the fresh food we hand out from about 72,000 pounds a year to about 81,000, an increase of about one-eighth. We based this goal on last season's offers. The farms have not promised a specific amount, and harvests vary. Whatever we bring in, we will report it to you honestly. If we fall short, we will explain why.

**Who will run it**

We are entirely volunteer-run, with 23 regular volunteers. Four of them have committed to driving the van on a weekly schedule.

**Cost and sustainability**

The van costs $68,000. We are asking the Foundation for $50,000, and the remaining $18,000 will come from our reserves. We estimate insurance and fuel at about $4,500 a year. [How this will be paid.]

**Our record with the Foundation**

In 2023 the Foundation granted us $12,000 for shelving. Our final report on that grant was four months late. Our treasurer at the time was in the hospital for most of that period, and we should have had someone ready to step in.

For this grant, our treasurer, Dave Lin, will be responsible for the final report and will submit it within 30 days of the end of the grant year. We will also send the Foundation our fresh food totals every quarter, so you can follow the van's results throughout the year.

**Why this matters**

Local farms are already offering us fresh food. With this van, we will be able to say yes when a farm calls.
</final_document>

**Before you send it:**

- **Running costs:** Reviewers will look for how you'll pay the $4,500 a year, so the bracketed sentence needs a real answer. That could be a budget line you'll add, a sponsor, or a fundraiser. If you don't have an answer yet, it's better to say you're working on one than to leave the sentence out. Maintenance and registration aren't mentioned because you don't have those numbers. Add them if you can get them.
- **Cold storage:** I left out any claim about storage because you need to check. If the produce can't be kept cold once it's unloaded, a reviewer will spot that gap. Find out before you submit. If you do have cooler space, one sentence saying so will strengthen the application.
- **Drivers:** Check whether a van this size needs a special licence or an insurance check for volunteer drivers. Your insurer will probably ask about it anyway.
- **Things I didn't include:** The $11,000 left in reserves isn't mentioned, because without knowing how many months it covers, it raises a question the narrative can't answer. The farm letters are described as attached, so check that the application allows attachments.
